angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 523,862 km at 183.35 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4540 +/- 0.0159 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 183.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.753 +/- 0.051 solar radii from Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of NGTS-35 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract): 523,862 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.789 +/- 0.035 solar masses from Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of NGTS-35 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4717 +/- 18 K from Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of NGTS-35 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kendall et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of NGTS-35 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ngts-35.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.582, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
